author_notes: Slot slot_169 targets the unused demo007x/golang-blog Editor.md static editor documentation bundle under static/editor. The repo is deterministic under a simple HTTP server after the SiteContinuum static entry detector recognizes docs/index.html from the project root. The task upgrades an almost-empty generated JSDoc home into a genre-native Documentation index: a section navigator whose tabs filter a grid of cards linking to the real editormd.js source listing, example and KaTeX pages, language packs, plugin template, preview CSS themes, and browser test fixtures, with a live 'Showing N of 7' readout. The interactive section filter, responsive tab wrapping, JSDoc typography, and preserved source code listing keep the change grounded in real repo assets and images across desktop, tablet, and mobile states.

problem_statement: The demo007x/golang-blog workspace serves the Editor.md static editor bundle under static/editor. Its generated JSDoc docs route is technically runnable and the repo ships a rich set of real assets: editormd.js, example pages, language packs, plugins/plugin-template.js, preview CSS, browser fixtures, fonts, and documentation scripts. However, the JSDoc home page is almost empty and the source page has no layout-level bridge back to the surrounding project assets, so readers see a generated source listing with no way to navigate the docs. Modify the existing JSDoc HTML/CSS layout so the docs home becomes a filterable Documentation index: a section navigator whose tabs (All, API, Examples, i18n, Extend, Test) filter a grid of cards that link to the real repo routes and a live readout reports how many sections are shown. Clicking a section tab must re-filter the grid AND update the readout count. Carry the same Documentation index context onto the source page. Preserve the original JSDoc identity, generated footer, source listing for editormd.js, examples pages, KaTeX example, and static serving across desktop, tablet, and mobile states.
required_content: Turn docs/index.html into a Documentation index: a section navigator with tabs All, API, Examples, i18n, Extend, Test filtering a grid of route cards, using real DOM text (not comments or hidden-only labels).
The completed UI should include visible text equivalent to Documentation index, Source API, Examples gallery, Language packs, Plugin template, Preview themes, and Test fixtures.

Each card links to an existing repo file/route including docs/editormd.js.html, examples/index.html, examples/katex.html, languages/en.js, plugins/plugin-template.js, css/editormd.preview.css, and tests/codemirror-test.html.
Clicking a section tab filters the grid to that section AND updates a live readout in the form 'Showing N of 7 · <Section>' (e.g. clicking Examples shows 'Showing 2 of 7 · Examples').

Add matching Documentation index context to docs/editormd.js.html while preserving the Source: editormd.js heading, @version v1.4.5 metadata, Open source online markdown editor description, and code listing.
Keep examples/index.html and examples/katex.html reachable and visually stable, and keep desktop/tablet/mobile docs states readable without horizontal overflow.
Implement the change with existing static HTML/CSS/JS files without new dependencies, placeholder copy, static screenshot substitution, or external-only content.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the Documentation index on the JSDoc home across viewports; the section tab row must wrap without horizontal overflow.
desktop_source and mobile_source protect the top of the generated editormd.js source listing with the Documentation index context across viewports.
desktop_source_deep protects the code listing after scroll so the generated source is not truncated or screenshot-substituted.
desktop_examples and desktop_katex_example protect the sibling example pages reachable from the index cards.
desktop_examples_filter protects the section filter: clicking the Examples tab must filter the grid to 2 cards and update the readout to 'Showing 2 of 7 · Examples'.
